title: Cultural Disorientation
description: Assess the 'Culture Shock' of your current environment. Discover if you are adjusted or just drifting.

questions.text: Walking down the street in my host city, I feel...

options.text: At home and comfortable.
Like a resident.
Like a tourist who hasn't left yet.
Like a ghost; I don't belong in this landscape.

questions.text: The unwritten social rules of this country (manners, humor, pace) feel...

options.text: Easy to follow.
A bit confusing, but I'm learning.
Exhausting; I'm always on guard for a faux pas.
Hostile; I feel like I'm constantly breaking invisible laws.

questions.text: I find myself romanticizing my home country and ignoring its flaws...

options.text: No, I have a balanced view.
Occasionally, when I'm sad.
Often; everything was better there.
Constantly; my host country is a prison compared to 'Home'.

insight_cloud.title: Cultural Mourning
insight_cloud.text: Moving to a new culture involves 'unresolved grief'. You are mourning the loss of a thousand micro-stabilities (the smell of the air, the way people stand in line). It's a real psychological loss.

options.text: Satisfying and real.
Functional.
Superficial; I have no real local friends.
Distant; I only talk to other expats/immigrants.

questions.text: Do you feel like your 'values' are coming into direct conflict with your new society?

options.text: No.
Rarely.
Often, and it hurts my integrity.
Yes, I feel like I'm losing my moral compass.
